texts.value: Catalyzes the hydrolytic deamination of adenosine and 2-deoxyadenosine
Binds 1 zinc ion per subunit.
Inhibited by reagents such as p-chloromercuribenzoate, and by coformycin, a structural analog of inosine
Optimum pH is between 6.9 and 8.5 for both adenosine and 2-deoxyadenosine.
Belongs to the metallo-dependent hydrolases superfamily. Adenosine and AMP deaminases family. Adenosine deaminase subfamily

Catalyzes the reversible phosphorolytic breakdown of the N-glycosidic bond in the beta-(deoxy)ribonucleoside molecules, with the formation of the corresponding free purine bases and pentose-1-phosphate (PubMed:11786017, PubMed:21672603, PubMed:235429, PubMed:30337572). Acts on 6-amino and 6-oxopurines including deoxyinosine, deoxyguanosine, deoxyadenosine, adenosine, guanosine, and inosine (PubMed:11786017, PubMed:21672603, PubMed:235429, PubMed:30337572). Does not act on xanthosine (Probable). May also catalyze a phosphate-dependent transfer of the pentose moiety from one purine base to another (PubMed:235429)

a purine 2'-deoxy-D-ribonucleoside + phosphate = a purine nucleobase + 2-deoxy-alpha-D-ribose 1-phosphate

texts.value: Optimum pH is 7.1 for deoxyinosine as substrate (PubMed:235429). Optimum pH is 7.5 for inosine as substrate (PubMed:235429). Optimum pH is 8.2 for hypoxanthine as substrate (PubMed:235429).
Homohexamer; trimer of homodimers
Belongs to the PNP/UDP phosphorylase family

Purine salvage pathway enzyme which catalyzes the transfer of the ribosyl-5-phosphate group from 5-phospho-alpha-D-ribose 1-diphosphate (PRPP) to the N9 position of hypoxanthine to yield IMP (inosine 5'-monophosphate). To a lesser extent, can also act on guanine leading to GMP, but shows a highly less efficient activity with xanthine
Inhibited by the product IMP (PubMed:12070315). Highly inhibited by nucleoside phosphonates, which are product analogs (PubMed:23927482, Ref.6)
kcat is 59.0 sec(-1) with hypoxanthine as substrate. kcat is 10.2 sec(-1) with guanine as substrate. kcat is 0.008 sec(-1) with xanthine as substrate (at pH 8.5 and 25 degrees Celsius).
Purine metabolism; IMP biosynthesis via salvage pathway; IMP from hypoxanthine: step 1/1
Homotetramer

E.coli cells express two distinct 6-oxopurine PRTases, with very different specificities for hypoxanthine, guanine, and xanthine. Salvage enzymes allow a more energy efficient synthesis of purine nucleoside monophosphates compared with the de novo pathway. The kinetic analysis suggests that E.coli HPRT is mainly responsible for the synthesis of IMP and that XGPRT primarily salvages guanine and xanthine
Belongs to the purine/pyrimidine phosphoribosyltransferase family

Purine salvage pathway enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of the ribosyl-5-phosphate group from 5-phospho-alpha-D-ribose 1-diphosphate (PRPP) to the N9 position of the 6-oxopurines guanine and xanthine to form the corresponding ribonucleotides GMP (guanosine 5'-monophosphate) and XMP (xanthosine 5'-monophosphate), with the release of PPi. To a lesser extent, also acts on hypoxanthine (PubMed:3886014, PubMed:9100006). Does not ribophosphorylate adenine (PubMed:3886014)

Inhibited by thioguanine, GMP and, to a lesser extent, by thioxanthine, azaxanthine and azaguanine (PubMed:3886014). Highly inhibited by nucleoside phosphonates, which are product analogs (PubMed:23927482)
kcat is 112.0 sec(-1) with guanine as substrate. kcat is 150.1 sec(-1) with xanthine as substrate. kcat is 54.8 sec(-1) with hypoxanthine as substrate (at pH 8.5).
Purine metabolism; GMP biosynthesis via salvage pathway; GMP from guanine: step 1/1
Purine metabolism; XMP biosynthesis via salvage pathway; XMP from xanthine: step 1/1
Homotetramer

E.coli cells express two distinct 6-oxopurine PRTases, with very different specificities for hypoxanthine, guanine, and xanthine. Salvage enzymes allow a more energy efficient synthesis of purine nucleoside monophosphates compared with the de novo pathway. The kinetic analysis suggests that E.coli HPRT is mainly responsible for the synthesis of IMP and that XGPRT primarily salvages guanine and xanthine
Belongs to the purine/pyrimidine phosphoribosyltransferase family. XGPT subfamily

source_dispositions: PW002069/SMP0002081 legacy label I has four-reaction chemistry of MetaCyc PWY-6609 III. Do not label-match P121-PWY or equate SMP0002084 (different route) to current III.
All four native MetaCyc reactions, all three predecessor links and all 17 Rhea sides retained. Rhea protonation species are not exactMatch claims for older generic native compounds.

PathBank biochemical reactions 6047/6049/6050/6052 corroborate complete four-step chemistry. Its added PurP transport is contextual to the selected MetaCyc four-reaction metabolic boundary; no transport event or membrane crossing is fabricated.
The native PathBank Gpt controller is retained but expanded with independently verified Hpt, whose preference for hypoxanthine is supported by current reviewed protein and primary evidence.

Native reaction objects also expose alternative PpnP/XapA and cross-species enzymes. This graph represents the complete DeoD/Add/Hpt-Gpt route supported by the selected E. coli source, not an exhaustive catalogue of all proteins that can accept each substrate; no exclusive-enzyme claim.
Direct adenine-to-AMP, nucleoside hydrolase and Gsk inosine-kinase branches are distinct pathways; no steps from them are silently appended or claimed covered.
Add Zn binding/count remains HAMAP similarity inference. No Ca2+ cofactor inferred from the 1975 dialysis buffer; Hpt/Gpt Mg evidence has independently explicit enzyme/structure support.
Gpt earlier apparent trimer versus later tetramer evidence is preserved; current supported tetramer retained.

Synthetic analog inhibitors, non-route Gpt/Hpt substrate activities and broad transcriptional control omitted from this bounded native route. IMP product inhibition retained because the product is a local route node.
Multiple protein localization annotations are retained at their original IDA/HDA/IEA tiers, without assigning exclusive pathway localization.
The source pathway lists MG1655 but older experiments establish K-12 derivative context rather than MG1655-specific physiology; record taxon is K-12.
The 1975 figure is a broader purine map; only its independently native-defined four-step subroute supports this record, not de novo, histidine or downstream GMP steps.
